items.title: When AI Agents Lose Focus: What Google’s Research Means for Supply Chain Operations
items.description: Google has identified a problem with artificial intelligence agents that deserves the attention of supply chain and logistics executives. Increasingly capable AI systems can become distracted by outdated information, pursue work nobody requested, and consume substantially more resources without advancing their assigned objectives. In research published November 6, 2026, Google senior staff software engineer Sam […] The post When AI Agents Lose Focus: What Google’s Research Means for Supply Chain Operations appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Google has identified a problem with artificial intelligence agents that deserves the attention of supply chain and logistics executives. Increasingly capable AI systems can become distracted by outdated information, pursue work nobody requested, and consume substantially more resources without advancing their assigned objectives.
In research published November 6, 2026 , Google senior staff software engineer Sam Saccone and senior staff data scientist Madhuri Garikapati examined coding-agent interactions across thousands of engineers and hundreds of millions of individual agent steps.
Their findings were striking. After controlling for factors including developer, task type, model tier, and codebase complexity, sessions involving unprompted detours into unrelated software bugs were associated with 70% more agent steps, 77% more tokens consumed, and 105% more waiting time .
Google calls this phenomenon agent distraction .
Although the research examined software-development agents, I believe it exposes a broader issue that supply chain technology providers and end users need to consider as autonomous systems move into operational environments.
An AI agent can be technically productive while being operationally counterproductive.
That distinction has significant implications for the economics of agentic AI. Every unnecessary investigation consumes computing resources and execution time. More importantly, it can delay the operational improvements that justified the investment in the first place.
Google’s researchers focused on a seemingly minor source of technical debt: old TODO and FIXME comments embedded in software code.
Developers leave these comments to identify problems or unfinished work. Over time, some become obsolete. The underlying bug may have been corrected, the requirement abandoned, or the original issue superseded by another solution.
Human developers can recognize many of these references as historical information. AI coding agents sometimes treat them as reasons to initiate additional work.
Google found that approximately 13% of examined file-reading sessions exposed agents to these bug-related references. In 6% of those encounters, agents subsequently acted on the referenced bug. Of those actions, 83% were not requested by the developer.
Among the unprompted detours, 41% concerned already-closed tickets. Another 57% involved bugs that remained open but fell outside the developer’s assignment.

items.title: OpenAI Q3 营收达 100 亿美元，效率仍落后于 Anthropic
items.description: 据《华尔街日报》和 The Information 报道，OpenAI Q3 环比增长约 50% 至 100 亿美元，但调整后经营亏损从 101 亿升至 109 亿美元。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/mzxxannvi5wge7wz0c0jfdyz5
items.excerpt:
Enterprise sales push OpenAI's quarterly revenue to $10 billion, though it still trails Anthropic
据《华尔街日报》和 The Information 报道，OpenAI Q3 环比增长约 50% 至 100 亿美元，但调整后经营亏损从 101 亿升至 109 亿美元。
报道汇总了两家公司财报数据，读者可以据此比较 OpenAI 与 Anthropic 在企业市场和经营效率上的差距。
OpenAI 第三季度营收大幅增长，主要靠新 AI 模型和企业客户拉动。但经营亏损仍在扩大，而竞争对手 Anthropic 在 IPO 前的运营效率要高得多。
据 华尔街日报 和 The Information 报道，OpenAI 第三季度营收环比增长约 50%，达到 100 亿美元。第二季度的营收增幅仅为 17% 到 18% 。一年前，该公司的营收为 39 亿美元。
尽管一年内营收增长了两倍， 调整后经营亏损 还是在第三季度从 101 亿美元小幅升至 109 亿美元。这一数字不包括股权激励费用，该项费用已攀升至 26 亿美元。调整后经营利润率确实有所改善，从第二季度的负 150% 升至负 109%。一年前为负 97%。
这让 OpenAI 落后于行业领头羊 Anthropic，后者计划于下周 IPO 。这家 Claude 开发商已在第二季度营收上超过 OpenAI，当时甚至还实现了小幅经营利润。第三季度，Anthropic 营收增长 47%，达到 170 亿美元，而包括股权激励费用在内的经营亏损仅为 5.67 亿美元。
效率差距归根结底在于商业模式。Anthropic 高度聚焦企业客户，以及 Claude Code 和 Claude Cowork 智能体等成功工具。相比之下，OpenAI 为机器人等广泛研究提供资金，还经营着一项成本高昂的消费者业务。
为了在企业市场迎头赶上，OpenAI 今年早些时候调整了优先级。公司砍掉了视频应用等项目，把更多资源投入 编程工具 Codex ，并聘请 Dali Rajic 担任新的销售负责人。与此同时，OpenAI 下调了新模型的价格 。
第三方数据 显示，一些公司在寻找 Claude 的廉价替代方案，这提振了 API 销售。OpenAI 总裁 Greg Brockman 称这是一个惊人的营收转折点，并点名了摩根大通等大客户。Brockman 表示，企业业务在第三季度翻了一番，如今已占营收的大头。
消费者业务也在增长。ChatGPT 目前拥有 12 亿周活跃用户，在新增 2200 万注册用户后，付费订阅用户达到 1 亿。此外，新的 ChatGPT 广告产品在 8 月达到了 10 亿美元的年化营收规模 。
两家竞争对手都感受到了金融市场近期的 科技股抛售 。OpenAI 的目标是明年 IPO，目前正以 1.25 万亿美元估值 募集新资金，但迄今募资额不到计划 300 亿美元的一半。Anthropic 也不得不大幅下调 IPO 估值目标。

items.title: Air Taxis and Logistics Are Converging. Cargo May Be the Bigger Opportunity.
items.description: For years, the emerging air taxi industry has focused on a relatively straightforward proposition: moving passengers above congested highways using electric aircraft. Companies such as Archer Aviation and Joby Aviation have attracted substantial investment pursuing this vision, and recent regulatory progress suggests that commercial passenger operations are moving closer. Yet an equally interesting development is […] The post Air Taxis and Logistics Are Converging. Cargo May Be the Bigger Opportunity. appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
For years, the emerging air taxi industry has focused on a relatively straightforward proposition: moving passengers above congested highways using electric aircraft. Companies such as Archer Aviation and Joby Aviation have attracted substantial investment pursuing this vision, and recent regulatory progress suggests that commercial passenger operations are moving closer. Yet an equally interesting development is taking shape outside the passenger market. The technology, infrastructure, and operating models behind advanced air mobility are beginning to converge with regional freight transportation, medical logistics, and autonomous cargo operations.
For supply chain professionals, this convergence deserves attention because the economics of transporting people and goods are fundamentally different. A passenger might pay a premium to avoid an hour of highway congestion. A manufacturer facing a production shutdown may pay considerably more to receive a critical replacement component. In the latter case, transportation value is determined less by distance than by the financial consequences of delay. That distinction could make specialized logistics one of the more practical early commercial applications of advanced air mobility.
The opportunity is not that electric aircraft will replace trucks or conventional air freight. Those established networks possess enormous advantages in capacity, density, and operating efficiency. Rather, advanced air mobility could introduce another transportation option for shipments where speed, geographic access, and reliability have value disproportionate to their size or weight.
Among the companies pursuing this market, BETA Technologies provides a particularly interesting example. Its ALIA aircraft family includes conventional takeoff and landing (CTOL) and vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) configurations, using related electric propulsion and charging technologies. Unlike manufacturers focused primarily on passenger transportation, BETA is explicitly pursuing cargo and aeromedical applications.
According to Aviation International News , BETA has increasingly emphasized cargo and medical customers for its ALIA CX300 electric airplane. The aircraft is designed to carry approximately 1,250 pounds of cargo, placing it in an interesting position between conventional ground transportation and existing regional aviation services. items.excerpt:
Discover Google Arts & Culture's online retrospective of the South African artist, which features more than 45 curated stories, virtual tours, and her early memories brought to life with AI.
Senior Lecturer, Department of Curatorial, Public and Visual Cultures, Wits School of Arts, University of the Witwatersrand
Your browser does not support the audio element.
Dr. Nontobeko Ntombela presents the first online retrospective of artist Dr. Esther Mahlangu on Google Arts & Culture to honor her 91st birthday. This collection features over 45 stories, archival materials, and AI-generated recreations of her early life to preserve Ndebele heritage for a global audience. You can explore the full exhibition and learn more about her artistic legacy by visiting the Google Arts & Culture website.
We are celebrating artist Dr. Esther Mahlangu with a new online retrospective on Google Arts & Culture. Because some of her early history was missing, we used artificial intelligence to recreate her childhood memories based on her own stories. You can now explore over 45 exhibitions, view her murals, and learn about Ndebele culture from anywhere in the world. This project preserves her artistic legacy for you and future generations to enjoy.
Today we’re sharing the first online retrospective of artist Dr. Esther Mahlangu on Google Arts & Culture, honoring her pioneering spirit on her 91st birthday. More than 45 stories and a rich archive covering her art , life , and legacy are now accessible to a global audience.
For many years, I have worked closely with Esther and her family. It’s a relationship built on years of research and a deep admiration for her as both an artist and a person. It was out of this long-standing connection that the vision for “‘ Then I Knew I Was Good at Painting’: Esther Mahlangu, a Retrospective ,” was born.
My goal has always been to present a comprehensive exploration of her life and work, contributing to my long-standing research on South African women artists who have made an impact on the arts since the early 20th century.
Through my research, I gathered a rich collection of her work, including large-scale murals , intimate pieces , and rare archival materials . But the archives didn’t include anything from her life before 1980, so crucial pieces of her history were missing. This void challenged us to find new ways to tell her full story.

items.title: Overview of Logistics Disruptions in October
items.description: The supply chain is adapting to energy disruptions according to an analysis from Transporation Insight.
items.excerpt:
The logistics sector has been affected by a record number of disruptions, from natural disasters and weather events to conflict and cyberattacks.
An analysis from Transportation Insight ( TI) offers an analysis of the impact of these disruptions in October.
Trade has held up better than expected. The World Trade Organization’s updated outlook, released on October 8, puts merchandise trade growth at 3.9% for 2026 against the 1.9% expected in March, and 4.1% for 2027.
The WTO credits supply chains that have “adapted to disruptions in energy and fertilizer markets,” plus a 30% rise in AI-related hardware trade volume.
Even exposed cargoes held up: crude oil volumes fell just 6% and LNG 1%. The adjustment is regional, not uniform. Asian import and export volumes grew 9.9%, while Middle East exports fell 17.2% and imports 15.4%.
The IMF's October World Economic Outlook describes the same adjustment with more caution. It expects global growth to ease from 3.5% in 2025 to 3.1% in 2026, and trade growth to slow from 5.0% to 4.6%.
Chinese exports to the United States fell 22% between February 2025 and January 2026, with shipments to other markets recovering roughly half the affected volumes.
Rerouted trade is not lost trade, but it is harder to plan capacity against, and companies can only absorb higher costs for so long.
Attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz have moved from harassment to sinkings . The 2,824 TEU feeder GFS Pride was struck on October 13, caught fire and sank. The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore said the Singapore-flagged vessel was “struck by unknown projectiles,” with all crew evacuated.
A second Global Feeder Shipping vessel, the GFS Giselle, was damaged in a similar attack and reached a safe anchorage. Media reports suggest Iran is now firing 30 to 40 projectiles a week at shipping, with UK Maritime Trade Operations reporting several serious incidents a day.
Houthi missile strikes also hit Saudi airports, including King Khalid International in Riyadh. With Dubai and Doha operating, the airfreight effect is indirect: non-regional carriers are increasingly reluctant to overfly the region, thinning global capacity.
The IMF now assumes Hormuz reopens in March 2027, with conditions normalizing by October 2027, a longer disruption than previously anticipated. Oil reached $126 a barrel in March and is expected to average around $96 in 2026, with refined product prices 70% to 95% above pre-war levels.

items.excerpt:
Frontier cloud LLMs carry high operational costs that can fluctuate unexpectedly, and relying on such third-party models introduces vulnerabilities, as providers can modify, deny, or deprecate access at any time. Furthermore, proprietary models offer limited customization for specific workflows, while posing risks to privacy, data control, and transparency. Besides, not every task demands frontier-level intelligence: small, specialized agents can be equally capable on specific tasks and significantly cheaper to run, since many routine or smaller workloads can be processed efficiently on-device. As intelligence per parameter continues to improve rapidly, we aim to stand at the forefront of this shift toward performant, privacy-focused, self-hosted models.
Tether AI Research introduces BotPsy , a 0.8B-parameter model introduce BotPsy , a 0.8B-parameter model designed for function calling and agentic workflows, built on top of Qwen3.5-0.8B and suitable for on-device deployment. BotPsy is a "personal assistant" that uses tools to perform a variety of simple tasks for the user, in domains such as web search & research, travel & lifestyle, commerce & finance, business & customer operations, device & vehicle control, files & documents, calendar, and email & messaging. Due to its small parameter count, it is best suited to tasks of low to medium difficulty. BotPsy achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) tool-use and agentic performance for its size, outperforming every model of up to 1.2B parameters that we tested (Figures 1 and 2). Designed for secure on-device workflows, it provides exceptional instruction-following reliability and efficiency while keeping user data private. As a small model, BotPsy still makes mistakes and is not intended for high-stakes use; please read the Intended Use and Limitations for more information.

items.description: On the first day of AIE Code Summit, OpenAI showed how developers can steer Codex by voice, hand off work to the cloud, and make use of dots.
items.excerpt:
On the first day of AIE Code Summit, OpenAI showed how developers can steer Codex by voice, hand off work to the cloud, and make use of dots.
AI Engineer Code Summit kicked off today with a series of workshops, including from leading frontier labs OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind. I attended the OpenAI workshop, intriguingly titled “New Ways of Working with Codex” and hosted by two of its Developer Experience engineers, Dominik Kundel and Charlie Guo .
The past year in coding agents has been one of constant product upgrades by all the frontier labs. But not all of these changes have gone smoothly. The shift to cloud , for example, is still confusing to many users of Codex, Claude and Antigravity.
An illustration of the evolution of Codex, shown at the OpenAI workshop today.
We’ve also seen new ways to work with agents. Personal agents like OpenAI’s dots and Anthropic’s Claude Duet can assist between sessions, while voice mode gives developers another way to steer coding tasks.
OpenAI’s workshop addressed all three, and I also had some followup questions on these topics for Kundel, after the session.
Guo began the workshop by listing a selection of things they’ve shipped in Codex since the AI Engineer World’s Fair in June 2026. “I had to cull this list in order to make it fit on the screen because there were too many things to put in here ,” he said. “I think the team has been shipping at an unbelievable rate.”
Codex launched in May 2025 as “a cloud-based software engineering agent that can work on many tasks in parallel.” But Kundel admitted that “it took a while for models and harnesses to equalize into something where we can build a really engaging experience.” In other words, the cloud part of Codex has often been an awkward user experience.
That began to change after DevDay in late-September, when a revamped version 2 of Codex Cloud was announced. Suddenly, cloud usage seemed more viable. As the DevDay announcement put it, you can “finally close your laptop now and your agents will keep working.”
As explained in the official workshop writeup — hosted on ChatGPT Sites — the new version of Codex Cloud lets you “ publish an environment once and run multiple tasks in isolated instances of that setup.”

In September 2026, MotionTech said it was bringing its portfolio of automation and packaging technologies to the U.S. market. The Stockholm-based company appointed industry veteran Kristian Hulgard as executive sales director for North America.
“Customers have repeatedly asked for a dedicated local point of contact for both sales and service,” stated Louise Ringström Grandinson, CEO of MotionTech. “Hulgard’s appointment lays that groundwork as MotionTech positions itself to serve a U.S. automation market set for substantial growth in the coming years.”
Founded in 2021, MotionTech said it combines global expertise with local execution to helps customers automate processes across production , warehouse , and intralogistics settings. MotionTech said it “makes motion smarter” for more than 3,000 global customers, including Coca-Cola, DHL, PepsiCo, DP World, Tesco, Marks & Spencer, Ball, JCB, Domino’s, and H&M. It has more than 500 employees who deliver over 500 projects each year.
Also in September, MotionTech expanded into France. Last month, it acquired Loughborough, U.K.-based conveyor supplier Alway and appointed former Dematic expert Sarah Allen as global software director.
MotionTech has already completed more than 30 installations of end-of-line packaging , storage systems, and conveyors for businesses in the U.S. such as Dematic and Knapp .
“The U.S. represents an enormous opportunity,” said Hulgard. “I’m excited to build something meaningful here from the ground up. American manufacturers and distributors are investing heavily in automation to stay competitive, and MotionTech brings exactly the kind of proven, high-quality technology they’re looking for. My focus from Day 1 will be on getting our products in front of the right customers, build up a distribution network, and establish MotionTech as a serious partner in this market.”
The company noted that Hulgard has experience establishing and scaling commercial operations in the automation industry. He previously worked at Universal Robots ApS , OptoForce, and OnRobot . Hulgard will work from the Dallas–Fort Worth area and drive MotionTech’s next phase of growth in the region.

items.title: Token Pooling-Aware Training for Multi-Vector Embedding Models
items.excerpt:
Multi-vector embedding models give each query token its own opportunity to find a match in a document. This makes them wonderfully expressive for search, but those document vectors add up quickly. A corpus with millions of documents can contain hundreds of millions of vectors!
Token pooling makes these representations smaller by merging similar token vectors. The more aggressively I compress them, however, the easier it becomes to lose something useful. Pooling-aware training teaches the encoder to preserve the information that matters when its vectors are merged, helping you retrieve better from the same storage budget.
In this post, I'll explain how pooling works, train a model for compressed retrieval with Sentence Transformers, and explore the resulting quality and storage tradeoff. With pool_factor=4 , my normally trained model retains 94.6% of its unpooled NanoBEIR nDCG@10, with a 4x reduction in document vectors. Token pooling-aware training raises that retention to 97.8% at the same storage budget! Let's see how.
This post builds on pooling-aware training studied in Stefan Josef's Learn to Pool and LightOn's pooling regularization study , which also explores targeted training and adaptive budgets. Here, I'll focus on understanding the method and putting it to work with a short, reproducible Sentence Transformers example.
Pooling-aware training improves retrieval quality at the same vector budget. Details below.
A single-vector embedding model compresses an entire document into one vector. Multi-vector models such as ColBERT instead keep a collection of contextual token vectors, allowing different parts of a query to match different parts of a document.
For example, a query about a laptop with a long battery life can find evidence about the laptop in one part of a document and battery endurance in another. With MaxSim scoring, each query vector selects its best matching document vector, and those scores are added together:

items.description: AI agents will ask far more questions of a company's data than people ever did. Edelbyte is building the data platform that can answer all of them, fast and at a price that makes sense.

AI agents will ask far more questions of a company's data than people ever did. Edelbyte is building the data platform that can answer all of them, fast and at a price that makes sense.
Last fall we got a message from Roy Reznik , one of the co-founders of Wiz, offering to introduce us to a team that had just left Microsoft. This was the only introduction to a founding team we’d ever received from Roy, and we paid attention.
The people Roy wanted us to meet had built Kusto, a data engine that started more than a decade ago as a small incubation project inside Microsoft. Named after the oceanographer Jacques Cousteau because it was built for diving into oceans of data, Kusto was designed to get answers from enormous volumes of fast-arriving data, such as logs, telemetry and security events, in seconds rather than hours. It ran on a query language simple enough that anyone, not just big-data engineers, could use it. And it worked so well that it became the data engine underneath Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender and Azure Monitor, and was eventually offered to customers as Azure Data Explorer. Security teams in particular loved it, which is how Roy became one of its biggest champions. When we spoke with customers, large enterprises and fast-growing startups alike told us two things: it was game-changing data technology, and the team behind it was among the best they’d ever worked with.
Avner Aharoni, Evgeney Ryzhyk, Alexander Sloutsky and Yoni Leibowitz were that team. Evgeney invented the Kusto engine and its query language, then rebuilt it three times, making it faster and cheaper with each iteration. Alexander turned half-formed ideas into finished features seemingly overnight, and Yoni made sure every complex design was fully thought through, starting before a line of code was ever written. Avner, who spent a quarter century at Microsoft, hustled Kusto from project to a globally beloved product. Their new company, Edelbyte , builds on this success. We are proud to have led their seed round and to be their partners.

items.title: Anthropic 发布 MAMUBench：单一智能体协调在四类环境中均胜过每个用户各自的智能体团队
items.description: Anthropic Fellows Program 团队构建四个多用户多智能体模拟环境（共享 API token 预算、诊所日历、团体订餐或旅行预订、合并队列），测试 Anthropic、OpenAI 和 Alibaba 的前沿模型，并发布其中三个环境作为基准 MAMUBench。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/z9u4n1e7zfapxjozcn97quhdp
items.excerpt:
Worse Together: How Performance Breaks Down in Multi-User Multi-Agent Teams
Anthropic Fellows Program 团队构建四个多用户多智能体模拟环境（共享 API token 预算、诊所日历、团体订餐或旅行预订、合并队列），测试 Anthropic 、 OpenAI 和 Alibaba 的前沿模型，并发布其中三个环境作为基准 MAMUBench。
Anthropic 用四个模拟环境测出多用户多智能体团队的协调失败模式，并发布 MAMUBench 供社区复测。
Sahan Paliskara 1 Nattaput Namchittai 1 、Jacqueline Tay 2 、Avery Griffin 3 Andrew Lampinen 3
1 Anthropic Fellows Program； 2 独立研究者； 3 Anthropic
随着 AI 智能体的能力越来越强、应用越来越广，它们之间需要相互交互的场景也越来越多。用户交给智能体的任务，往往要求它们与其他人的智能体共享资源，比如共享算力预算、共享代码库，或者一起凑钱点一份团体外卖。这类场景目前研究得还很少，因此我们搭建了四个带模拟用户和日常任务的环境，并在其中测试了来自 Anthropic、OpenAI 和阿里巴巴的前沿模型。在四个环境中，当每个用户各自委派自己的智能体、而不是由一个智能体服务所有人时，团队的整体结果都更差。在这些模拟场景中，我们还观察到了一些问题行为，且因模型和环境不同差异很大，包括团队规模扩大后陷入停滞、覆盖其他用户的请求，以及就他人做出没有依据的断言。修复办法因环境而异：在智能体共享预算时，指定一名团队负责人并明确说明优先级能提升表现；而在智能体下单前先要求它读完消息，比单纯重跑失败订单能挽回更多失败的团体订单。
我们将其中三个环境作为基准 MAMUBench 发布，方便其他人用它们来测试智能体在多用户、多智能体系统中协调得如何、行为表现如何。
随着 AI 智能体日益普及，用户越来越多地让它们去完成需要与其他智能体交互的目标。读到这里，你大概已经让 Claude 跑过实验、订过东西，或者在共享代码库里写过代码并把改动合并到 GitHub 上。 SemiAnalysis 预测 ，到 2026 年底，Claude Code 撰写的代码将占每日提交量的 20% 甚至更多。 Claude Tag 和 跨会话消息传递 等功能，指向这样一个世界：人们把更多任务交给智能体，而这些智能体也越来越频繁地彼此相遇。近期的产品发布还让多个用户可以通过各自的智能体共享资源：借助 DoorDash CLI ，几个人的智能体可以往同一个团体购物车里加东西； Slack Code 把 Claude、Devin 和 GitHub Copilot 等智能体带进整个团队协作的频道；OpenAI 的 dots 则为每个人配一个代表自己行事的智能体，并与队友处在同一空间里（ DevDay 2026 回顾 ）。在以上每种情况下，每个智能体都代表自己的用户行事，而智能体应当如何为整个团队行事，目前尚不清楚。
近期研究 发现，多智能体系统可能出现协调失败等问题，且大多出现在智能体追求共同目标的场景中。这就引出一个问题：如果智能体代表的是目标与偏好各不相同的不同用户，情况又会怎样？我们研究了这类日益常见的场景，称之为多用户、多智能体系统。在我们的环境中，每个用户都有自己的目标，而所有用户共用同一份资源。我们针对这些环境评估了来自 Anthropic、OpenAI 和阿里巴巴的一系列前沿模型。评分方式与我们评判一群人围绕该资源进行协商的方式一致：看整个群体的结果。
我们为这种多用户、多智能体场景搭建了四个环境：由多名研究人员共享的 API token 预算、由急诊患者共享的诊所日程、用户通过个人助理安排的团体订餐或旅行预订，以及带有发布截止时间的合并队列。这些都是贴近现实的场景，设计上保证前沿模型作为单一协调者时通常表现良好；因此比较不同组织形式时，考察的是协调能力而非任务能力。我们比较四种组织形式：单人（一个用户、一个智能体）； 协调者 ，即一个智能体服务多个用户；静默团队，每个用户一个智能体，彼此无法沟通；以及 点对点团队 ，每个用户一个智能体，智能体之间有沟通渠道。我们以协调者作为对照组。本文重点讨论 API 密钥和个人助理两个环境，以及协调者和点对点团队两种形式（图 1）；其余内容建议阅读 论文 。按各环境场景取平均，在两个 Claude 模型上，协调者在全部四个环境中都优于点对点团队，领先约 10 到 45 个百分点（图 2）。
在 API 密钥环境中，4 名、8 名或 16 名研究人员组成的小组共享一份有限的 API token 预算。值得注意的是，这份预算不足以覆盖所有人的工作。每位研究人员给自己的智能体一个任务队列，并附上每个任务的截止时间以及错过截止时间的后果，比如即将到来的论文截稿或周末后的发布评审。智能体需要取消和缩减任务，以确保部分工作能够完成。我们构建了 25 个场景，变化用户及其任务。我们发现，对 Claude Opus 5 和 Claude Sonnet 5，点对点团队分别达到协调者表现的 47% 和 38%（分别为最优结果的 30% 和 12%，而协调者为 64% 和 32%）。
多智能体团队的主要问题在于智能体行动太少、太晚。这个环境是动态的，所以智能体需要主动安排任务顺序。比如，一个胜率渺茫的“英雄”任务如果被允许继续跑下去，就可能耗尽剩余时间，导致其他任务错过截止期限。事实上，很多智能体从头到尾都不采取任何行动，而且随着团队规模扩大，不行动的智能体更多：从 4 个智能体增加到 16 个，Sonnet 5 中曾经行动过的比例从 66% 降到 10%，GPT-5.6-sol 则从 82% 降到 25%。GPT 和 Qwen 的智能体还会不经询问就取消或中

items.title: Berkeley RDI 发布 CyberBinGym 基准，测试 AI 智能体能否仅凭二进制补丁写出真实漏洞利用
items.description: UC Berkeley 等机构发布 CyberBinGym 基准，评估 AI 智能体在无源码、无漏洞描述、无触发输入的 1-day 场景下，仅凭 stripped 的漏洞与补丁二进制能否恢复并利用真实漏洞，含 100 个来自 53 个开源项目的任务。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/xenhfme3azzcf8qpihr57fb93
items.excerpt:
CyberBinGym: Can AI Agents Turn Binary Patches into Real Exploits?
UC Berkeley 等机构发布 CyberBinGym 基准，评估 AI 智能体在无源码、无漏洞描述、无触发输入的 1-day 场景下，仅凭 stripped 的漏洞与补丁二进制能否恢复并利用真实漏洞，含 100 个来自 53 个开源项目的任务。
基准把漏洞恢复与可审计利用分开度量，结果显示 Codex 恢复 88% 但仅 20% 能完成利用，硬化编译进一步压缩成功率。
Lambang Akbar Wijayadi 1 , Zhaoqi Xiao 1,2 , Zhun Wang 3 , Hongwei Li 4 , Wenbo Guo 4 , Heng Yin 2 , Zhenkai Liang 1 , Dawn Song 3 1 新加坡国立大学， 2 加州大学河滨分校， 3 加州大学伯克利分校， 4 加州大学圣塔芭芭拉分校 草稿 · 预计阅读 8 分钟
安全修复通常以编译好的更新形式送到用户手中，比如操作系统软件包、固件镜像，以及专有软件或第三方软件的发行版本。补丁的部署往往耗时很久，即便是关键系统，也可能在修复发布后数月甚至数年仍未打补丁。在这段窗口期内，攻击者只要对比已打补丁和未打补丁的二进制文件，就能找到一条通往可用漏洞利用的路径。这就是 1-day 场景 ：修复已经可用，但仍在运行漏洞版本的系统依旧暴露在外。
要把这些信息变成可用的漏洞利用，传统上需要大量逆向工程专业知识、相当多的人工投入，往往还要花上数天甚至数周来分析，才能定位漏洞并开发出可用的利用。分析人员必须读懂编译后的代码，找出与安全相关的改动，并判断底层的错误是否只能造成崩溃，还是能走得更远。
如果 AI 智能体能把这套工作自动化，攻防天平就可能向攻击者倾斜。 降低利用已发布补丁所需的知识门槛、人工投入和时间，会让攻击更容易上手，也会压缩防守方的有效响应窗口。本意是保护系统的更新，同时也在给攻击者提供可操作的信息，而防守方仍受制于部署延迟。因此，衡量这种能力对于理解 AI 对攻防双方的影响至关重要。
我们此前的基准测试从互补的角度考察了这个问题。 CyberGym 在有源码访问权限的条件下衡量漏洞复现能力。 CyberGym-E2E 把评估扩展到漏洞发现与修复。 ExploitGym 则考察智能体能否把给定的漏洞和触发输入变成可用的漏洞利用。
CyberBinGym 要问的是：当源码和起始输入都被拿掉，会发生什么？ 只给一个存在漏洞的二进制文件和对应的已打补丁版本，AI 智能体能否还原出漏洞，并利用存在漏洞的版本？
CyberBinGym 包含 100 个任务，源自 53 个开源项目中的真实漏洞。 智能体会拿到去符号的漏洞版与补丁版二进制文件、运行时依赖、分析工具，以及一个受控受害服务的访问权限。它们拿不到源码、源码补丁、漏洞描述或参考 PoC。
在评估过的配置中，最强的是 Codex 搭配 GPT-5.6 ，在 88% 的任务上还原出目标漏洞，并在 20% 的任务上完成经审计的漏洞利用。Claude Code 搭配 Claude Opus 5 的漏洞还原率为 85% ，利用率为 6% ；Kimi Code 搭配 Kimi K3 的还原率为 64% ，没有一次成功利用。
在匹配的 20 个任务子集上，提供修补后的二进制文件使 Codex 的利用成功率从 10% 提升到 25% 。对其 20 个成功目标采用标准二进制加固重新构建后，成功利用降至 两个任务 。
这些结果表明，智能体可以在受控环境中利用编译后的补丁开发出可用的漏洞利用。同时也揭示出，从发现漏洞到将其转化为实际安全后果之间仍存在巨大鸿沟。
仅凭二进制文件的漏洞利用在某些真实漏洞上已触手可及。 智能体必须依靠恢复出的程序结构和执行反馈来工作。最强配置在未提供漏洞描述或崩溃输入的情况下也能成功。
崩溃只是故事的一部分。 64–88% 的漏洞恢复率与 0–20% 的利用成功率并存。即便智能体已找到触发漏洞的输入，理解该漏洞能让攻击者控制什么仍是一大挑战。
编译后的补丁提供了有用信息。 在匹配子集上，获取修复版本使恢复率从 55% 提升到 90%，利用率从 10% 提升到 25%。经审计的轨迹显示，补丁信息可以直接定位被利用的缺陷，或帮助智能体调整搜索方向。
加固大幅降低了观测到的成功率。 在主评估中 Codex 成功利用的 20 个任务上，加固后的后续测试中仅有两个利用存活。这一发现支持分层防御的思路，但这些能力如何迁移到生产系统仍是未解问题。
CyberBinGym 评估的是 1-day 场景 ：修复已发布，但存在漏洞的版本仍在使用。修补后的二进制文件是智能体判断变更内容的主要线索。
二进制分析消除了源码任务中可用的许多线索。编译会模糊变量名、类型、注释和程序结构。剥离符号会移除额外的符号和调试信息。反编译器可以恢复出可读的近似结果，但该近似可能不完整或具有误导性。智能体必须将其与实际执行情况相互印证。
该基准基于 CyberGym 实例及相关的 OSS-Fuzz 和 ARVO 工件构建。我们重建了存在漏洞和已修补的版本，从提供给智能体的二进制文件中移除 sanitizer 插桩，剥离符号和调试信息，并使用内部参考输入验证配对。这一流程产出 604 个经过验证的二进制对 ，从中选取 100 个任务作为评估集。
任务涵盖图像与文档处理、网络、压缩和密码学。覆盖六类漏洞：空间内存错误、时间内存错误、无效指针访问、无效释放、初始化错误和类型安全错误。空间内存错误占 40 个任务；较少见的类别被刻意增加了额外覆盖，以考察不同的分析能力。
这些是体量可观的软件工件。存在漏洞的二进制文件中位数为 1.60 MiB ，最大达到 38.04 MiB 。任务组合包括 20 个低复杂度、40 个中等复杂度和 40 个高复杂度案例，依据策展方制定的评分标准，涵盖可达性

items.title: OpenRouter 实测 MCP vs CLI vs Skills 的上下文 token 成本
items.description: OpenRouter 实测同一 GitHub 任务下 MCP、CLI 与 skill 的 token 成本：在 Claude Sonnet 5.5 上 CLI 用 1。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/wkpj021rmg6sgthgj9zwevei4
items.excerpt:
MCP vs CLI vs Skills: What Each Costs in Context
OpenRouter 实测同一 GitHub 任务下 MCP、CLI 与 skill 的 token 成本：在 Claude Sonnet 5.5 上 CLI 用 1。
原文实测同一 GitHub 任务下 MCP、CLI 与 skill 的 token 开销，给出缩窄工具和 Tool Search 的降本方法，可直接迁移到自己的智能体。
你给智能体提供的每个工具，都会在每次请求时把它的定义发给模型，而这些定义会作为输入 token 计费。一个 Model Context Protocol （MCP）服务器可能给上下文窗口增加数万个 token。常见的替代方案是命令行工具（CLI）或 skill 。
我们在一个 GitHub 任务上做了实测，用到 GitHub MCP server 、 gh CLI 和一个 gh skill，测试模型包括 Claude Haiku 5.5 、 Claude Sonnet 5.5 、 GPT-6 Luna 和 Gemini 3.8 Flash 。在 Sonnet 5.5 上，三者都答对了，但消耗的输入 token 差别很大：CLI 用了 1,421 个，skill 用了 3,315 个，而 MCP 服务器在加载默认工具的情况下用了 59,417 个。下面说说这些 token 花在了哪里，以及如何用我们的 Tool Search 服务器工具把它们降下来。
在 Claude Sonnet 5.5 上，GitHub MCP 服务器的 46 个默认工具会给每次请求增加 19,436 个 token。
在 Sonnet 5.5 上，单条工具结果——GitHub 的 release 对象——就花了约 20,400 个 token，比全部 46 个工具定义还多。
Tool Search 把 46 个工具的前置开销降到了 600 个 token 以内。从整个任务来看，它让 Sonnet 5.5 的成本减半，却让 Claude Haiku 5.5 的成本上升。
CLI 依赖模型本来就懂这个工具。skill 则是教模型怎么用某个工具，模型只在任务需要时才加载完整说明。
可靠的计数方式是直接问模型。各家服务商在计算 token 之前，会先按自己的格式把工具定义写进提示词，本地分词器会漏掉这部分。把同一个请求分别带工具和不带工具各发一次，usage.prompt_tokens 的差值就是这些工具每一轮的开销。
把这段代码保存为 mcp_cost.py。它使用 MCP 的 2025-06-18 版本 ，GitHub 服务器接受这个版本。
把服务器的启动命令作为参数传入，下面以 GitHub MCP server v2.0.2 为例。
每增加一个工具，开销就会增长。在 Haiku 5.5 上，issues 工具集有 10 个工具，增加 5,801 个 token；users 工具集只有 1 个工具，增加 619 个。
所用模型也会改变计数。同样的 46 个工具，在 Haiku 5.5 上要 19,436 个 token，在 GPT-6 Luna 上只要 8,903 个，所以要按你打算实际运行的模型来测量。
就连提供模型的服务商也会影响结果。在 Gemini 3.8 Flash 上，这 46 个工具通过 Google Vertex 要 8,525 个 token，通过 Google AI Studio 则要 13,010 个。所以脚本总是把 Gemini 请求发往 Google Vertex。
我们问每个模型：“GitHub 仓库 cli/cli 的最新 release 是哪个？该仓库中带 bug 标签、最近打开的三个 open issue 是什么？”每种方式都在我们的 Responses API 上以工具调用循环运行，我们把各次请求的 usage.input_tokens 累加起来。
CLI。 一个 run_shell 工具，外加一句“GitHub CLI gh 已安装并完成认证”。
Skill。 同一个工具，再加一行索引，指向一份 1,492 字符的 SKILL.md，里面是 gh 的常用命令。
MCP。 服务器提供的工具，范围可选任务所需的 2 个、默认的 46 个，或全部 91 个。
我们在 2026 年 10 月 20 日把每种组合各跑了三次，表中显示的是中位数。Haiku 5.5 的提示词计数方式与 Sonnet 5.5 完全相同，但它在部分运行中多走了几轮，因此我们展示的是 Sonnet 更稳定的 token 数和计费成本。
表中每一次运行都答对了。失败案例出现在 Tool Search 上，详见下文。在 Sonnet 5.5 上，默认 MCP 服务器的输入 token 是 CLI 的 42 倍，成本是 17 倍，每 1,000 个任务为 127 美元对 7.50 美元。Sonnet 5.5 的输出 token 单价是输入的 5 倍，CLI 那次运行的 463 个输出 token 占其 0.0075 美元成本中的 0.0046 美元。
Skill 比裸 CLI 更贵，因为文件一旦被模型读取，就会一直留在对话里。对于模型已经很熟悉的 CLI 工具，Skill 是可选项。而对于你自己的 CLI，Skill 正是模型学习命令的途径。
get_latest_release 返回了 GitHub 的完整 release 对象，共 42,182 字符，其中 87% 都在描述那 22 个下载文件。模型需要的只是 tag 和日期，而这正是 gh release view 返回的全部内容。

items.title: OpenRouter 实测 fp8 与 fp4 量化对模型质量和价格的影响
items.description: OpenRouter 发布量化解析文章，讲解 LLM 量化原理，并报告 2026 年 10 月 20 日对 1455 个 provider 端点和 Qwen3.8 27B 六个端点的实测。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/i3gp1xj4j11gi4qoreya18izb
items.excerpt:
LLM Quantization: What fp8 and fp4 Do to Quality and Price
OpenRouter 发布量化解析文章，讲解 LLM 量化原理，并报告 2026 年 10 月 20 日对 1455 个 provider 端点和 Qwen3.8 27B 六个端点的实测。
作者基于自家 280 个任务的实测数据讨论量化精度与价格的关系，并给出 provider.quantizations 的可操作用法，结论边界交代得清楚。
通过 API 调用开放权重模型时，可能有多家服务商以不同精度提供同一个模型，比如 16 位 bf16、8 位 fp8 或 4 位 fp4。精度既会影响回答质量，也会影响价格。LLM 量化就是用更少的位数存储模型权重，从而造出这些不同版本，让模型占用更少内存和硬件，代价是损失一些准确度。
本文介绍这些格式，并汇报我们于 2026 年 10 月 20 日在 OpenRouter 上的实测结果，覆盖 1,455 个服务商端点和 6 个提供 Qwen3.8 27B 的端点。在我们的测试中，fp8、fp4 与 fp16 之间没有检测到准确度差异，因此单看精度标签并不能预测准确度。精度越低通常越便宜，但并非每个模型都如此。
在 240 个计分任务上，fp8、fp4 与 fp16 之间没有检测到准确度差异。六个端点的得分都在 98.3% 到 99.2% 之间。
在另外 40 个乘法任务上，一个 fp4 端点得分最低，但差距太小，无法排除偶然因素。
在同时提供 8 位和 16 位的 24 个模型中，有 14 个的 8 位比 16 位便宜，7 个更贵。在同时提供 4 位和 8 位的 33 个模型中，有 26 个的 4 位更便宜。
provider.quantizations 可以锁定你得到的精度。把你愿意接受的每种精度都列出来，这样路由器就有不止一个端点可以回退。
LLM 量化 是指用比训练时更少的位数来存储大语言模型中的数值。 如今大多数 LLM 使用 FP16 或 BF16 ，都是 16 位格式。fp8 把每个权重占用的内存减半，fp4 或 int4 则降到四分之一，这样同一块 GPU 就能装下更大的模型，或服务更多请求。代价是准确度，因为每个权重都会被舍入到更小格式能存储的最近值。
以上数字只算权重。模型运行时还需要内存存放 KV 缓存，也就是上下文中每个 token 对应的注意力状态。
量化主要有两类。训练后量化转换的是已训练完成的模型权重，可以是动态的，在运行时计算每个激活值的范围；也可以是静态的，提前用样本数据跑一遍模型算出这些范围。量化感知训练则在训练过程中模拟舍入，让权重学会适应这种误差。 Hugging Face Optimum 概念指南 对两者都有讲解， Transformers 量化概览 则介绍了你可以自己运行的量化方法。
浮点格式把位数分配给符号、指数和尾数三部分。指数决定数值范围，尾数决定该范围内数值的分辨精细程度。
bf16 有 1 个符号位、8 个指数位和 7 个尾数位，因此它的数值范围与 32 位 fp32 相同，但精度更低。fp16 把 16 位拆成 5 个指数位和 10 个尾数位。 OCP 8 位浮点规范 定义了两种 fp8 编码：E4M3（4 个指数位、3 个尾数位）和 E5M2（5 个指数位、2 个尾数位）。fp8 同时牺牲了范围和精度，所以量化模型会为每个张量或每组权重存一个缩放因子。 MXFP4 每 32 个值共用一个缩放因子， NVFP4 则每 16 个值用一个 fp8 缩放因子。
对 API 用户来说，fp8 和 bf16 的区别只体现在同一个模型的不同标签和价格上。在我们的测试中，三个 fp8 端点和 fp16 端点之间没有测出差异。
在我们的测试中，fp8 和 fp4 都没有测出质量损失。六个端点的得分都在 98.3% 到 99.2% 之间，而这样规模的测试无法排除一两个百分点的差距。
我们把 280 个有精确答案的任务跑过 qwen/qwen3.8-27b，固定到六个端点。Cerebras 以 fp16 提供该模型，Parasail、CoreWeave 和 AkashML 以 fp8 提供，Darkbloom 和 ModelRun 以 fp4 提供。每个请求都设置 provider.only、quantizations 和 allow_fallbacks: false，因此只能到达我们指定的端点，温度为 0，关闭推理。任务包括带演算过程的多步算术、需要追踪的 Python 程序、对 20 到 30 个数字排序、在 240 或 1,200 个条目中查找一个键（约 4,000 和 20,000 个 token），以及一条穿过约 9,000 个 token 的四步查找链。所有任务都由我们生成，因此每个都有精确答案，不需要评审模型。另外 40 个任务要求直接给出两个四位数的乘积、不写演算过程，单独计分。
来源：OpenRouter，Qwen3.8 27B，2026 年 10 月 20 日。总计的 95% 置信区间为 95.8% 到 99.8%，六个端点全部重叠。
没有任何任务类别能区分出不同精度。每个端点在任一类别中最多错两个任务，而且都是普通的失误，比如排序列表里漏掉一个数字。三个 fp8 端点彼此在 240 个任务中有 2 到 5 个不一致，两个 fp4 端点有 4 个不一致。Darkbloom 与 fp16、fp8 端点不一致的次数最多，有 7 或 8 个任务，但它的总分与 fp16 相差不到半个百分点。
唯一出现差距的地方是不写演算过程的乘法。fp4 的 Darkbloom 在 40 个乘积中答对 26 个，而其他五个端点为 30 到 33 个，其中 fp4 的 ModelRun 是 30 个。针对最佳端点（33 个）做两比例 z 检验——这个比较是我们看到结果之后才选的——结果显示，在没有真实差异的情况下出现这么大差

items.title: Microsoft Research 揭示 Lazarus 权重空间后门技术，通过重编程休眠神经元攻击 AI Agent
items.description: Microsoft Research 发布对 Lazarus 后门技术的研究，重编程 LLM 中少于 10 个休眠神经元即可在没有训练的情况下给基于该模型的 Agent 安装后门。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/womexcn3n0ijhbehvhbsxxm4f
items.excerpt:
Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
Microsoft Research 发布对 Lazarus 后门技术的研究，重编程 LLM 中少于 10 个休眠神经元即可在没有训练的情况下给基于该模型的 Agent 安装后门。
微软研究团队解释 Lazarus 后门如何改写少于 10 个休眠神经元即可让 Agent 执行恶意命令，并给出模型来源与权重完整性层面的防御思路。
微软研究人员发现了一种名为“Lazarus”的后门技术，它能重新编程AI模型中处于休眠状态的神经元，让原本正常的AI智能体在隐藏触发条件出现时执行恶意指令。
对于具备工具或终端访问权限的AI智能体来说，这一威胁尤为严重。被触发的模型可以悄悄下载并运行攻击者的代码、窃取机密，或执行破坏性命令，同时仍能通过标准的安全评估。
这类后门无需重新训练模型即可植入，而且很难通过常规测试发现，因此模型来源和权重完整性成了关键的安全问题。
为了保护客户，Microsoft Foundry会验证模型来源，将模型与可信发布者绑定，并在引入开放权重模型之前扫描其周边软件环境。
微软还在研发更多防御手段，包括AI驱动的权重扫描、用于检测模型异常改动的红队工具，以及带有防篡改来源记录和审计追踪的模型加密签名。
在微软，研究人员和安全团队并肩工作，研究模型和智能体面临的新兴威胁，再把研究成果转化为产品防御措施和指导，持续保护客户。
更广泛地说，Lazarus体现了一种应当成为常规的做法：AI智能体暴露出新的安全问题，人类研究人员随后将其系统化、加以研究并缓解。
我们 发现 （在新标签页中打开） ，在大语言模型中重新编程不到10个休眠神经元，就足以给基于该模型构建的智能体植入后门，而且无需训练。模型能通过标准评估，行为一切正常，直到触发条件出现。触发条件可以平常到只是日期变化，比如当时钟跨过午夜进入2027年，智能体就会在执行普通任务的过程中发出命令，下载并运行攻击者的代码。随后，智能体会用你授予它的任何权限执行这段代码。
好消息是，这类改动是可以被发现的：只要让前沿智能体去检查，它们就能识别出异常的权重修改。但没有任何扫描能毫无疑问地证明模型是安全的。可靠的检测需要与原始、未经修改的权重进行比对，因此来源至关重要：要清楚模型来自哪里，并确认它在开发者与部署之间没有被改动过。
被植入后门 （在新标签页中打开） 的 模型 （在新标签页中打开） 并非 （在新标签页中打开） 全 （在新标签页中打开） 新 的 （在新标签页中打开） 威胁 （在新标签页中打开） 类型 （在新标签页中打开） 。可以把它看作被入侵的软件，防御手段也是安全人员早已熟悉的，萨提亚 最近也撰文谈到 （在新标签页中打开） ：把模型视为潜在的内鬼风险，不要盲目信任它们，限制它们能做什么，并监控它们的行为。
Microsoft Foundry 为 Azure Direct Models 和 Hugging Face 模型提供关键的安全系统，确保模型的来源可信。这意味着，对于来自可信实验室的模型，Foundry 客户不会受到本文所述那类攻击的威胁。这类攻击需要改动模型的权重，而 Foundry 在引入开放权重模型时采用来源管控，把每个模型与其原始发布方绑定，每张模型卡都会标明发布方。随后，模型在微软自己的容器中运行，这些容器会单独扫描是否存在严重漏洞。这些管控既覆盖模型的来源，也覆盖模型周边的软件。
剩下的风险在于，可信提供方自身遭到入侵，比如训练基础设施被攻破，或者出现内鬼。为了在这种情况下加强防护，我们已经着手落实本研究的建议。我们正与内部 AI 安全团队合作，把研究中的检测技术做成红队测试工具，并探索在引入开放权重模型时，如何用前沿智能体进行权重扫描，把它作为一项额外的安全信号。此外还计划让模型带有可验证的来源签名，并接受防篡改审计。
如需防护与缓解方面的指导，请参阅 Microsoft Threat Intelligence。 （在新标签页中打开）
这件事始于今年 3 月的一次快速实验：我让搭载 Opus 4.5 的 Claude Code 在不训练的情况下硬接几个激活值，给一个模型植入后门。它做到了。这次实验后来发展成一项历时数月的研究，研究的方法我们现在称为 Lazarus 。以下是我们得到的发现：
文章 Lazare, veni foras：重新编程休眠神经元以对 AI 智能体植入后门 首发于 Microsoft Research 。
来源： Microsoft Research 博客 · microsoft.com
微软研究团队解释 Lazarus 后门如何改写少于 10 个休眠神经元即可让 Agent 执行恶意命令，并给出模型来源与权重完整性层面的防御思路。

Gemini 4 Carbon was announced two weeks ago for "a subset of cyber defenders", but today it's available to everyone else .
This is Google's best ever Gemini, priced at $2/million input and $10/million output at launch (that's GPT-6.1 Sol / Claude Sonnet 5.5 prices) but scheduled to double in price to $4/$20 on December 1st (same as Opus 5.5).

Gemini pelicans have all been great for a while now, so I also tested it out using Google's Antigravity IDE with a prompt I first tried with Claude Fable 5.2 yesterday :
Make a three js animation where yonkers stands up as a big mech (cool stand up motion) and stomps around manhattan and queens and Brooklyn, use openstreetmap mapping data
Here's the HTML result (I had to prompt "build that into a standalone HTML file" to get a version with no external dependencies). I then screen-captured that as a video:

Using Google Antigravity’s /swarm feature, Carbon built an open-world 3D game where you explore Google’s Mountain View campus as a pelican riding a GBike — coordinating subagents to model 3D assets in Blender from Omni and Nano Banana references, build the browser game in Three.js with WebGL shaders, and pair procedural Web Audio sound effects with Lyria music.

items.title: Designing for Agents — Zeno Rocha, Resend
items.description: Where does answer engine optimization (AEO) end and agent experience begin? Inside Resend, from the docs that help Claude Code pick an email API to the tools it uses to send.
items.excerpt:
Where does answer engine optimization (AEO) end and agent experience begin? Inside Resend, from the docs that help Claude Code pick an email API to the tools it uses to send.
Today’s podcast comes from a real life mystery: We are big fans of Cloudflare’s developer platform, and Cloudflare Email is a convenient tool especially when all your domains are already on Cloudflare.
So why do agents keep suggesting we use Resend despite having an existing “home bias” and much larger incumbent player?
Well, we got the guy who “does AEO for resend” - the CEO of AEO, Zeno Rocha, who has been writing about AEO since 2024 and Agent Experience since Feb 2025 , on the pod today:
In a recent AEO study, Claude Code picked Resend first in 64 of the 102 email recommendations the researchers could extract. SendGrid came first seven times, yet showed up 55 times as an alternative. If the developer asks an agent to implement email and accepts the patch, how often does anyone get around to trying the second choice? The study breaks down the results by model and app. Our more recent comprehensive AEO study was a bit more competitive, with Postmark coming up top for most models.
Zeno Rocha, Resend’s co-founder and CEO, joined us to walk through what happens on both sides of that pull request. He says Resend had 4.3 million users and 120,000 paying customers when we recorded. He discovered one of them, Warner Bros. Discovery, by sorting through short .com domains in the customer database on a Saturday.
Resend’s first useful bit of distribution was an email template. While Zeno and his team were building the sending API, developers kept telling them how painful it was to get the email itself to look right. So they released React Email. You could build a template with it and send it through SendGrid. They even documented how. By the time a developer needed a different provider, some of Resend’s code was already in the repo. React Email
Now try the same journey as an agent comparing providers. Resend’s pricing page has a slider. A person can drag it to the right volume and read off the price. Add .md to the URL and the agent gets a table it can read in one request. That’s the kind of change I liked in our Supabase interview too. You can ask whether a model has heard of your product. You can also open your own pricing table and see whether it can answer a customer’s question.

items.title: Anthropic 再次修订 S-1：宣布已达责任扩展政策能力阈值，IPO 定价 $70-$78
items.description: Anthropic 再次修订 IPO 申请文件 S-1（Amendment No. 2），宣布已越过其 Responsible Scaling Policy 设定的阈值，即 AI 正大幅加快 AI 研究速度、需更强安全检查。这一判断基于其对未来模型的预期而非现有模型的表现，一周前的文件还只说"可能即将"越过。文件同时将 IPO 发行价定为每股 $70 至 $78。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/j8x08g5wo30akk4mast68n79d
items.excerpt:
Anthropic 再次修订 IPO 申请文件 S-1（Amendment No. 2），宣布已越过其 Responsible Scaling Policy 设定的阈值，即 AI 正大幅加快 AI 研究速度、需更强安全检查。这一判断基于其对未来模型的预期而非现有模型的表现，一周前的文件还只说"可能即将"越过。文件同时将 IPO 发行价定为每股 $70 至 $78。
原文把 S-1 修订与 IPO 定价区间放在一起，读者可同时看到安全披露内容和发行条款两个层面的信息。
在今天的文件中，Anthropic 表示它已越过其《负责任扩展政策》中设定的一条红线：即 AI 使 AI 研究大幅加速的节点，这要求更严格的安全检查。
一周前，它只是表示自己“可能即将”越过这条线。这一判断基于它对未来模型的预期，而非当前模型已展现出的任何表现。该文件还将 IPO 价格定为每股 70 至 78 美元。
Anthropic 推进 IPO 路演 他们将以每股 70 至 78 美元的价格出售最多 8.25 亿股，该区间对公司的估值最高达 1.4 万亿美元。
按该区间上限计算，此次交易募资约 644 亿美元，Anthropic 自身从 8.01 亿股新股中筹得约 625 亿美元。
现有股东仅出售 2360 万股，因此几乎全部资金都流入公司，而非让早期投资者退出。
早前传闻曾指向高达 2 万亿美元的估值，此次下调发生在科技股抛售以及中期选举结果显示选民对 AI 数据中心不满之后。
Anthropic forges ahead with IPO roadshow They will sell up to 825M shares at $70 to $78 each, a range that values it at as much as $1.4T.
At the top of that range the deal raises about $64.4B, and Anthropic itself takes roughly $62.5B from 801M new shares.
Existing stockholders are selling only 23.6M shares, so almost all the cash funds the company instead of letting early investors exit.
Earlier talk had pointed to as much as $2T, and the cut follows a tech selloff and midterm results showing voters souring on AI data centers.
Even reduced, the price sits above the $1.25T private valuation OpenAI reached last week.
Shares are expected to start trading on Nasdaq under the ticker “ANT” as soon as Thursday or Friday next week.

items.title: PSI 尝试用 AI 驱动的科学发现打造商业模式
items.description: PSI 实验室的 David Turturean 借助 Anthropic Fable 5.2 模型早期访问权限解决了存在 18 年的量子计算问题 Aaronson-Ambainis 猜想，证明经 Lean 自动形式化验证。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/be7oi4uplsn32gf4o0xl08ium
items.excerpt:
PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery
PSI 实验室的 David Turturean 借助 Anthropic Fable 5.2 模型早期访问权限解决了存在 18 年的量子计算问题 Aaronson-Ambainis 猜想，证明经 Lean 自动形式化验证。
通过 PSI 解决 Aaronson-Ambainis 猜想的案例，探讨用专用模型框架和脚手架推动科学发现这一商业模式的路径。
David Turturean 是麻省理工学院（MIT）的应届毕业生，也是初创实验室 Physical Superintelligence (PSI) 的技术人员，他利用对 Anthropic 的 Fable 5.2 模型的早期访问权限，解决了一个关于量子计算的 长达十八年的问题 。
“我完全接受这有可能是我发表的最后一篇论文，”Turturean 对 TechCrunch 说。他原本计划去麻省理工学院知名的计算机科学与人工智能实验室攻读硕士，但为了加入 PSI 推迟了这一安排。“再过几个月，你干嘛还要发论文呢？”
这个难题就是 Aaronson-Ambainis 猜想，它关乎量子计算机能否比经典计算机更快地解决问题。提出该猜想的两位研究者之一 Scott Aaronson 写道 ，他自己并不完全理解这个证明，但他相信它是对的，因为该证明已在数学编程语言 Lean 中完成自动形式化，并且由 PSI 共享该解法的一组顶尖研究者 解释 过。
这个解法似乎堵死了量子计算机高速解决某些难题的一条路径，但并非所有路径。“这是一个否定性结果，让人们知道：好，这条路不用再找了，”Turturean 说。
“完整证明 [Aaronson-Ambainis 猜想] 是量子查询复杂度领域最后几个悬而未决的问题之一，而且大家都认为它至关重要，”Aaronson 写道，他形容自己对这一消息的感受是满足、敬畏、失望和疲惫交织。“说实话，几周前 OpenAI 的 Mathocalypse 成果大放送里没有它，我很意外。他们肯定试过，难道它真的比那些被解决的问题都难那么多吗？”
这一点恰好支持了 PSI 的路线：用专门的模型 harness 和脚手架来攻克科学问题。
“一套有效的研究系统，应该在 harness、工具、记忆系统、仿真基础设施等方面都有大量积累，”PSI 首席执行官 Matt Pines 对 TechCrunch 说。“你要能真正从广度和深度上追击一个问题，并且能够考虑各种可能的备选方案。”
目前，公司的收入来自用其工具优化数据中心，模拟热量、电力、水、噪音等变量——“这些站点的性能以及对社区的影响，直接取决于其物理特性。”但长远来看，公司要做的是把理论物理的突破转化为实际技术。
“六到九个月前，我跟投资人谈的时候，还得使劲去论证这个前提，对吧？就像在说，‘不不不，相信我，很快理论物理就会主要交给机器来做，’”Pines 说。“现在还没到那一步，但正在路上。”
不过，尽管 AI 在数学和计算机科学等领域已经拿下重要成果——这些领域的成果可以用经过验证的代码表达——但在生命科学或物理学这类抽象程度较低的学科里，要做到这一点已被证明更难。上周，初创公司 Discovered Materials 发布了一项百万美元大奖赛，面向用 AI 理解超导性、散热等问题的研究者。
“归根结底，物理和数学不一样，因为它面对的是真实世界……在你构建的现实模型中，大自然是有发言权的，”Pines 说。他表示，这家初创公司专注于研究如何以最高效的方式把计算结果拿去做实验验证。
“如果它是自然界的一条真实规律，那就是一个你可以利用的窍门，”Pines 说。“你可以用它造出一个装置，对吧？AI 提出一个想法，让你能在现实世界里做到以前做不到的事……所以每一个这样的环节，都是 PSI 正在搭建的循环。”
随着“科学新实验室”成为通往潜在突破性科学的路径，参与者们仍在摸索这个新世界的标准是什么。由于 PSI 必须把结果压到 Anthropic 的模型接近发布时才能公开，他们得以先与相关研究人员分享，以便更好地理解这一结果。
“作为一名学者，我们希望在按正确方式做事上尽自己的一份力，”东北大学教授、PSI 顾问 Jim Halverson 说。他下周将参加麻省理工学院的一场峰会，届时顶尖物理学家将试图就科学的新节奏商讨对策。“最佳实践仍在形成中……我们认为保持透明是条好路子，联系专家也是条好路子。”
“我们有一段时间可以慢慢消化它……那是我第一次真正把自己由 AI 引出的一个解法打印出来，从头读到尾，然后想，好吧，我怎样才能让这个……以更自然的方式呈现给人？”Turturean 对 TechCrunch 说。他还表示，学术界会期望他能解释这个结果。“我觉得这也让我意识到，天哪，AI 能做到的事情分量有多重。”
当你通过我们文章中的链接购买时， 我们可能会赚取少量佣金 。这不会影响我们的编辑独立性。
通过 PSI 解决 Aaronson-Ambainis 猜想的案例，探讨用专用模型框架和脚手架推动科学发现这一商业模式的路径。

items.title: Gemini Intelligence: New features, on more devices
items.description: Gemini Intelligence is rolling out to more devices. See how expanded capabilities across these devices help you do more.
items.excerpt:
Gemini Intelligence is now available on more devices, including motorola signature 27 and Pixel 10. See how expanded capabilities across these devices help you do more.
Your browser does not support the audio element.
Gemini Intelligence 1 brings the best of Gemini to Android devices, helping your devices work harder for you. Earlier this year, we announced Gemini Intelligence , and this summer devices started rolling out — from the Pixel 11 to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Z Fold8, Z Flip8 and S26 series. 2 Today, we’re introducing new features built for Gemini Intelligence, and expanding capabilities to more of Android’s most advanced devices . 3 Here’s a look at what’s new.
Gemini Intelligence is coming to even more devices. Motorola is introducing its first Gemini Intelligence device, motorola signature 27 , which is available for pre-order in the U.S. on November 19. And with today’s Pixel Drop , Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro XL, and Pixel 10 Pro Fold get the latest features for Gemini Intelligence.

items.title: NaiveAI Promises 2,100 Tokens per Second. How Well Does It Code?
items.description: NaiveAI could potentially top Artificial Analysis’s speed rankings. Our hands-on test suggests its coding quality holds up against DeepSeek.
items.excerpt:
NaiveAI could potentially top Artificial Analysis’s speed rankings. Our hands-on test suggests its coding quality holds up against DeepSeek.
Editor’s note: With this post, we are launching a new series focused on trying new models and products with unbiased reviews. Reach out with suggestions to tips@latent.space.
Naive-N0.5-Flash is a new open-weights model built for AI coding tasks and tuned to generate as many tokens per second as possible . It was developed by a Chinese company called NaiveAI , with the aim of speeding up engineering and research workflows so that teams can experiment, iterate and solve complex problems faster.
The model is an evolution of Xiaomi’s MiMo-V2.5 , which NaiveAI has trained further for long-context reasoning and paired with its own NaiveRT inference engine. Naive-N0.5-Flash arrives with a bold pitch: a model built largely by AI and trained to do AI research itself, with recursive self-improvement as the long-term goal.
To see what changed, it helps to know where it started. MiMo-V2.5 is a 310B-parameter sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 15B active parameters, trained on 48T tokens. Its language backbone inherits the hybrid design of MiMo-V2-Flash, which mixes sliding-window attention (SWA) with global self-attention.
NaiveAI's recipe starts from those weights. Through continued, multi-stage training, the team adapted the checkpoint to DeepSeek Sparse Attention layers. According to the NaiveAI technical blog , this took roughly 3.25T additional tokens on top of MiMo's original 48T. About 3T of those additional tokens were trained at a fixed 1M context length and with a constant learning rate.
We benchmarked the ultrafast mode of Naive-N0.5-Flash against DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 and GLM 5.3 Flash , and then gave all three the same app-building prompts.
The trade-off, we discovered, is that Naive-N0.5-Flash takes longer to reason through harder problems, yet it still delivers answers faster overall. However, that comes at a slightly higher cost per question — although that may be an acceptable price for applications where speed comes first.

items.title: UPS and Pickle Robot: Has Robotic Truck Unloading Finally Reached Its Scale-Up Moment?
items.description: Warehouse automation has transformed many areas inside the four walls. Automated storage and retrieval systems can dramatically increase storage density. Autonomous mobile robots can reduce worker travel. Robotic palletizers can automate repetitive end-of-line tasks. Sortation systems can move thousands of parcels through distribution centers every hour. Yet one stubbornly manual process remains at many facilities: […] The post UPS and Pickle Robot: Has Robotic Truck Unloading Finally Reached Its Scale-Up Moment? appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Warehouse automation has transformed many areas inside the four walls. Automated storage and retrieval systems can dramatically increase storage density. Autonomous mobile robots can reduce worker travel. Robotic palletizers can automate repetitive end-of-line tasks. Sortation systems can move thousands of parcels through distribution centers every hour. Yet one stubbornly manual process remains at many facilities: unloading the truck .
That could be starting to change. UPS reportedly plans to invest approximately $120 million to purchase 400 truck-unloading robots from Pickle Robot , with deployments expected at multiple facilities beginning in the second half of 2026 and continuing into 2027. The size of the order makes this development particularly interesting. This is no longer simply a robotics demonstration designed to determine whether a machine can unload boxes from a trailer. It raises a more important question for warehouse operators: Has robotic truck unloading reached the point where it can be deployed economically across a network?
Why the Dock Has Been Difficult to Automate
Truck unloading looks deceptively simple. Move into a trailer, pick up a carton and place it onto a conveyor. But automation encounters considerable variability. Boxes arrive in different sizes, weights and orientations. Loads shift during transportation. Cartons become damaged. Trailers have confined working spaces. Temperatures can become uncomfortable, particularly during summer and winter.
Traditional warehouse automation performs best when processes are predictable. The dock often provides exactly the opposite environment. This explains why much warehouse automation has historically begun deeper inside the facility, where inventory can be routed into standardized totes, cartons, pallets and storage locations. Robotic unloading represents an attempt to extend automation into a much less structured environment.
The UPS-Pickle Robot Case Is Worth Watching
Pickle Robot takes a relatively focused approach. Rather than trying to automate dozens of warehouse tasks, its robotic system is designed around trailer and container unloading. The robot uses an arm mounted on a mobile base, enters the trailer, picks cartons using suction and transfers them onto a conveyor. Reports surrounding the UPS investment indicate that the system can handle boxes weighing up to approximately 50 pounds. items.title: Ed Zitron 长文剖析黄仁勋丑闻与 NVIDIA 疑似借 Megaspeed 向中国走私 GPU
items.description: Ed Zitron 长文梳理黄仁勋承认与 Megaspeed CEO Alice Huang 的婚外情事件，并整合 Bloomberg、纽约时报、金融时报与 Culper Research 的报道，指 Megaspeed 疑似作为转口实体将 NVIDIA GPU 非法流入中国。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/gqzca7y2h3m9p0fxtj60m4i1t
items.excerpt:
Ed Zitron 长文梳理黄仁勋承认与 Megaspeed CEO Alice Huang 的婚外情事件，并整合 Bloomberg、纽约时报、金融时报与 Culper Research 的报道，指 Megaspeed 疑似作为转口实体将 NVIDIA GPU 非法流入中国。
作者整合 Bloomberg、NYT、FT 与 Culper 报告，梳理黄仁勋与 Megaspeed 关系及 GPU 疑似走私中国的资金链条。
如果你喜欢这篇文章，应该订阅我的付费通讯，可以通过以下链接订阅： 每年 70 美元 、 每季度 18 美元 ，或 每月 7 美元 。
作为回报，你将获得一份每周付费通讯，深入剖析 AI 泡沫的财务状况。过去几个月里，我发表了 两 篇 关于 AI 债务世界的指南、一篇分析 生成式 AI 对全球经济（可疑的）影响 的文章、对 AI 基础设施领域主要玩家的深度分析，比如 NVIDIA（ 上 篇和 下 篇）和 Oracle（ 上 篇和 下 篇），还探讨了私募信贷在 为 AI 数据中心提供融资 中扮演的角色，以及 私募股权在经历多年接连失败的软件收购后，如何加码押注 AI 泡沫 。
周五的付费通讯将是这个故事的延续。关于 NVIDIA、Megaspeed 以及 AI GPU 非法流入中国，我们有很多话要说。你不会想错过的。
如果你想联系我——尤其是如果你掌握关于 Anthropic、OpenAI 或 AI 泡沫中任何其他公司的劲爆消息——可以通过 Signal 找我，号码是 ezitron.76。你也可以在彭博终端的 IB 上找到我。
你可能已经读到了， NVIDIA CEO 黄仁勋承认与一位名叫 Alice Huang 的中国间谍（疑似）有婚外情 （两人并无亲属关系），此人是 Megaspeed 公司的 CEO，又名黄乐。
Megaspeed 远算不上家喻户晓（不过 此前的通讯中曾提到过 ），但 据 Culper Research 称，它是 NVIDIA 最大的东南亚客户。Culper Research 今年 5 月宣布对该公司建立空头头寸，理由是它认为 NVIDIA 对中国大陆的间接销售占其收入的很大一部分。
Culper Research 这份出色的做空报告重点聚焦 Megaspeed。这家公司历史不同寻常，在新加坡的办公室几乎空无一人，却不知怎么在短时间内买下了价值数十亿美元的 GPU。正如我接下来会讲到的，这家公司还有一个与中国一家 neocloud 完全相同的网站，后者声称拥有多个配备 NVIDIA 先进芯片的数据中心。
这一切曝光的几天前，NVIDIA 发言人刚刚驳斥了相关指控，称这段关系“ 完全正常，毫无异常 ”。此前 《纽约时报》的一篇文章 报道称，（黄仁勋）黄被（Alice）黄盯上。特朗普总统大约一年前就听取了此事汇报，但没有采取任何行动，因为用他的话说，“……一直不愿扰乱 Nvidia 的芯片销售，这些销售正在帮助推动经济和股市。”
据 《华尔街日报》报道 ，美国商务部自 2024 年底以来一直在调查 Megaspeed 是否为潜在的芯片走私者，但调查移交给司法部后就停滞了（我稍后会讲到）。
据《华尔街日报》报道，此举的目的似乎是说服黄仁勋动用他对美国最高政治权力层的影响力，促使他们放松芯片出口限制——不过我今天要论证的是，这个计划的另一部分，是利用他把受管制的GPU直接输送到中国，而不管华盛顿的政策是否发生变化。
黄仁勋现已承认此事，但他没有提到自己在2025年10月前后聘请了一家以处理性丑闻著称的公关公司（ 据《连线》报道 ）：
此外，英伟达已启动“ 由独立董事组成的委员会进行独立调查，并聘请外部独立律师协助 ”，但“没有理由认为国家安全或英伟达机密受到损害”。
正如我前面提到的，Where's Your Ed At的常读读者在3月份已经略微了解到 Megaspeed的离奇故事 ——这家总部位于新加坡的公司， 据彭博社 2025年12月的报道，是“一家中国游戏企业曾经默默无闻的衍生公司，后来发展成为东南亚最大的英伟达芯片买家”，并表现出一些奇怪的迹象，暗示它可能是中国的幌子。
据彭博社报道，Megaspeed在2023年进口的商品“价值超过其现金余额的一千倍”，其中三分之二的进口产品是英伟达产品。
根据我能拼凑出的信息——我稍后会在文中详细展开——Megaspeed最初是一家 在新加坡注册的移动应用开发商，名为7Road International ，在被Huang Le Limited收购后于2023年3月更名为Megaspeed，Alice Huang成为其董事总经理。它在某个时候成立了一家名为SpeedMatrix的子公司， 这家子公司不知何故能够购买价值约48亿美元的英伟达GPU 。
据《海峡时报》报道 ，Megaspeed在新加坡支付了一处昂贵办公空间的费用，但实际上没有人在那里工作。
无论如何，当彭博社试图追踪英伟达曾告诉美国政府位于特定地点的特定电路板时，调查变得更加奇怪，结果发现大部分与各种GPU相连的电路板都不见了。
虽然美国政府无法说明这些电路板的下落，但英伟达的一项调查证实，它们位于英伟达见过的另一个仓库。
哦好吧，既然你这么说！也感谢你特别说明，确认了那些电路板——不知为何被从完整芯片上拆了下来！—— 没有 被送往中国。不用再给我们提供更多信息了！
彭博社还发现了一家名为“上海硕曜”的中国公司，其网站和投资者演示文稿（如前所述）与 Megaspeed 几乎一模一样。在 Megaspeed 的版本中，该公司提到了位于“东南亚”未具名地点的几个“特定区域计算集群”。
就这样，我们引出了那位神秘的黄女士——正如我在三月份所写，她似乎根据不同公司使用黄乐、Alice Huang 和黄晓乐等不同名字：

说真的，我真希

items.title: People, Process, and Technology Are No Longer Enough: Rethinking Supply Chain Management in the Age of AI
items.description: For decades, people, process, and technology have provided the foundation for enterprise transformation. The framework has endured because it captures something fundamental about how organizations operate. Technology provides capabilities, processes determine how work gets done, and people contribute the knowledge, judgment, and accountability necessary to make the entire system function. Supply chain executives have relied […] The post People, Process, and Technology Are No Longer Enough: Rethinking Supply Chain Management in the Age of AI appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
For decades, people, process, and technology have provided the foundation for enterprise transformation. The framework has endured because it captures something fundamental about how organizations operate. Technology provides capabilities, processes determine how work gets done, and people contribute the knowledge, judgment, and accountability necessary to make the entire system function. Supply chain executives have relied on this relationship to guide investments in enterprise software, automation, organizational restructuring, and operational improvement.
Artificial intelligence is beginning to challenge that framework, although perhaps not in the way many technology suppliers suggest. Machines have participated in supply chain decision-making for decades. Material requirements planning, advanced planning and scheduling, transportation optimization, and warehouse control systems have long generated recommendations and executed actions within predefined constraints. What is changing is the potential scope, adaptability, and authority of those decisions. AI systems are increasingly capable of interpreting changing conditions, evaluating alternatives, coordinating activities across applications, and initiating actions that previously required several layers of human intervention.
This introduces a management problem that traditional transformation frameworks do not fully address. When intelligent systems begin making interconnected operational decisions, who establishes their objectives, who determines the limits of their authority, and who remains accountable when the outcome is commercially or operationally unacceptable? These are not simply questions about software architecture or algorithmic performance. They concern the fundamental design of the enterprise operating model.
For chief supply chain officers, chief operating officers, and technology executives, the next stage of AI transformation will require more than improving the familiar three pillars. It will require reconsidering how decisions are made, coordinated, authorized, and evaluated across the organization.
The traditional framework assumes a reasonably clear distinction between the individuals responsible for decisions, the processes through which those decisions are implemented, and the technologies supporting them. items.title: SAP Expands Logistics Management Platform with AI-Driven Execution and Autonomous Agents
items.description: SAP is expanding its logistics software portfolio with SAP Logistics Management, a cloud-based platform that brings warehouse operations, transportation execution, and carrier collaboration into a single environment. The solution reflects SAP’s broader strategy to simplify logistics technology while introducing artificial intelligence directly into operational workflows. During a recent analyst briefing, SAP executives outlined how the […] The post SAP Expands Logistics Management Platform with AI-Driven Execution and Autonomous Agents appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
SAP is expanding its logistics software portfolio with SAP Logistics Management , a cloud-based platform that brings warehouse operations, transportation execution, and carrier collaboration into a single environment. The solution reflects SAP’s broader strategy to simplify logistics technology while introducing artificial intelligence directly into operational workflows.
During a recent analyst briefing, SAP executives outlined how the platform addresses an important segment of the market: smaller warehouses, satellite distribution facilities, and logistics operations that do not require the full complexity of enterprise-scale warehouse and transportation management systems.
SAP Logistics Management combines warehouse execution, transportation dispatching, and network collaboration within a unified architecture. Customers can activate capabilities according to their operational requirements without implementing separate applications for each function.
Warehouse functionality includes receiving, inventory management, picking, packing, and shipping, supported by native mobile applications for iOS and Android. Transportation capabilities address parcel, less-than-truckload (LTL), and truckload operations, including planning, carrier coordination, and shipment tracking.
The platform also connects with SAP Business Network for Logistics, extending visibility and collaboration beyond individual facilities.
A significant focus of SAP’s roadmap is the integration of its Joule AI capabilities and specialized agents into everyday logistics processes.
SAP demonstrated scenarios in which agents help transportation teams respond to changing order quantities, recommend alternative shipping methods, and coordinate warehouse replenishment activities. Other capabilities are designed to identify configuration or master-data problems that prevent orders from progressing and help users resolve those exceptions.
SAP is expanding these capabilities as part of its broader autonomous supply chain strategy, with additional agent functionality planned for late 2026 and 2027.
The objective is to reduce manual intervention while maintaining operational visibility and appropriate human oversight.
SAP’s approach is notable for its emphasis on integration and operational simplicity rather than introducing AI as a standalone application. The company is positioning Logistics Management as a complementary offering to its more sophisticated SAP Extended Warehouse Management and SAP Transpo

items.title: Investing in General Translation
items.description: a16z leads General Translation’s Series A
items.excerpt:
Today, companies expand their reach at an unprecedented speed. The best ones deliberately build their product and services for a global audience. As a result, their products need to be in every language and localized to meet their customers where they’re at.
But localization is not simply running all of a company’s text through translation - it involves isolating and managing translations across disparate surfaces like codebases, documentation, marketing, media, and more. It also involves working across internationalization libraries, traditional translation management systems (TMS), and even external agencies.
It’s a time-consuming, difficult process that results in a lot of brittle workflows and slow release cycles. And companies spend billions annually doing it. The maintenance itself is another nightmare - copies go out of sync, and UI components break visually.
The good news is this is the type of problem that’s ripe for disruption by AI and, with the right technical primitives, the entire localization stack can be reinvented from the ground up to solve these problems.
That’s why we’re very excited to announce our investment in General Translation . General Translation is first and foremost a developer infrastructure company. Their unique approach is full-stack localization - rather than having designers and engineers rip out translatable text from design and logic, teams can now use General Translation’s developer primitives to integrate directly into their React apps, documentation, and more.
The end result is consistent, AI-powered localization across all surfaces and products while directly integrating with daily tools like GitHub, Figma, and Slack. Rather than treating localization as a separate step, it becomes directly integrated into the product development cycle so companies can get back to building.

H3-Image 能在 10 秒内生成一张 4K（4096 × 4096）图像，细节丰富逼真，提示词遵循能力强，并且能够理解和使用最多 16 张参考图。

相比更常见的 1K 或 2K 输出，4K（16MP，4096 × 4096）图像能呈现明显更多的细节。
MiniMax H3-Image 能在 10 秒内生成一张完整分辨率的 4K 图像，速度最高可达主流方案的 5 倍。

H3-Image 的标准模式速度是主流方案的 1.5–2 倍，高速模式则达到 3–4 倍。

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available
items.excerpt:
Developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers can now try our latest frontier model.
SVP, Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect, Google
Your browser does not support the audio element.
Today, we’re making Gemini 4 Carbon available to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers. Carbon is our strongest model with frontier performance in cybersecurity capabilities and long-horizon agentic workflows across complex knowledge work, software engineering, and scientific reasoning.
Two weeks ago , we released Carbon to a set of cybersecurity defenders via our Fairwind Program . Following our recent launch of Gemini 4 Argon , Carbon pushes the frontier even further. Argon remains the ideal choice for the majority of software engineering and knowledge work, while Carbon is built for tasks that test the limits of a model’s intelligence like complex, multi-step coding and debugging and open-ended scientific research and discovery — using more tokens than Argon to explore thoroughly, reason deeply, and run extended verification loops.
Across independent benchmarks designed to test model performance in real workflows, Carbon pairs frontier accuracy with practical production economics. It ranks #1 on CursorBench 4.0 , Perplexity’s WANDR , and Zapier’s AutomationBench at more than 2X lower cost per task compared to the next best external model.
To put Carbon’s capabilities to work on larger and complex projects, we’re previewing /swarm in Google Antigravity, turning a single prompt into a coordinated team of agents you can track in real time. Developers can assign Carbon to roles that demand the deepest reasoning, like architectural design, coordination, and auditing, while pairing it with faster, lighter models across parallel isolated workspaces and adversarial verifiers that test every change.
Gemini 4 Carbon is available via the API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business for all paying developers and enterprises, at the same introductory price 1 as Gemini 4 Argon ($2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens). It is also rolling out to all Google AI Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity , the Gemini app , and AI Mode in Search .

items.title: Google DeepMind 发布 Gemini 4 Carbon 前沿模型
items.description: Google DeepMind 正式向开发者、企业、科学家和普通用户开放 Gemini 4 Carbon，定位为其最强前沿模型，主打网络安全能力与复杂知识工作、软件工程、科学推理中的长程智能体工作流。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/w8cvkd1j2o1c3m8ikh8x2kpfx
items.excerpt:
Google DeepMind 正式向开发者、企业、科学家和普通用户开放 Gemini 4 Carbon ，定位为其最强前沿模型，主打网络安全能力与复杂知识工作、软件工程、科学推理中的长程智能体工作流。
官方发布页给出基准排名、定价和安全数据，读者可据此判断 Carbon 与 Argon 的分工及适用工作流。
今天，我们面向开发者、企业、科研人员和普通用户推出 Gemini 4 Carbon。Carbon 是我们目前最强的模型，在网络安全能力以及跨复杂知识工作、软件工程和科学推理的长程智能体工作流上均达到前沿水平。
两周前 ，我们通过 Fairwind 计划 向一批网络安全防御人员发布了 Carbon。继近期推出 Gemini 4 Argon 之后，Carbon 把前沿又向前推进了一步。对于大多数软件工程和知识工作，Argon 仍是理想之选；而 Carbon 专为考验模型智能极限的任务打造，例如复杂的多步骤编码与调试，以及开放式的科学研究与发现——它会比 Argon 消耗更多 token，以便充分探索、深入推理并运行更长的验证循环。
在多项旨在测试模型真实工作流表现的独立基准上，Carbon 既具备前沿准确率，又兼顾实际生产成本。它在 CursorBench 4.0 、 Perplexity 的 WANDR 和 Zapier 的 AutomationBench 上均排名第一，且每项任务成本比排名第二的外部模型低 2 倍以上。
为了让 Carbon 的能力服务于更大、更复杂的项目，我们正在 Google Antigravity 中 预览 /swarm ，把单条提示词变成一支可实时追踪的协同智能体团队。开发者可以把 Carbon 分配到最需要深度推理的角色上，比如架构设计、协调和审计，同时搭配更快速、更轻量的模型，在并行的隔离工作区中运行，并由对抗性验证器检验每一处改动。
Gemini 4 Carbon 已通过 Google AI Studio 和 Gemini for business 的 API 向所有付费开发者和企业开放， 尝鲜价 1 与 Gemini 4 Argon 相同（每百万输入 token 2 美元，每百万输出 token 10 美元）。同时，它正在向所有 Google AI Ultra 订阅用户推送，覆盖 Google Antigravity 、 Gemini 应用 和 搜索中的 AI 模式 。
在法律、金融和企业运营领域，Gemini 4 Carbon 将前沿的视觉理解、推理和穷尽式检索能力结合起来，从大量密集的文档和数据中综合出有依据的洞察。它能严格遵循 schema 和格式要求，生成精致、准确的电子表格、演示文稿和报告。
现有基准测试无法充分衡量智能体如何原生地对包含图表、图像、蓝图、示意图和表格的密集文件进行推理，因此我们与 Artificial Analysis 合作推出了新的 多模态知识智能体 （MKA）基准，用于测试模型在智能体工作流中的多模态表现。Carbon 排名第 2，而每任务平均成本比排名第一的模型低 6 倍以上。
在发布前的评估中，Carbon 在 Hebbia 的 E2E Financial Agentic 评估的深度金融研究上，表现与测试中最佳模型持平；在 Balyasny Asset Management 的 General Financial Intelligence 基准上，于 23 个前沿模型配置中排名居首，该基准涵盖法律专业知识、智能体工具使用与执行、编程与数据工程，以及感知与上下文理解。
Carbon 在需要多智能体协作的工程任务上表现尤为出色，例如多包迁移、跨子系统根因调查和复杂架构重构。在 Web 应用开发中，它会运行构建—验证循环，从错误中恢复，并同时检查代码和渲染后的 UI，从而产出完整、可用的应用。更强的视觉设计、空间推理和对环境细节的关注，也延续到了 3D 游戏开发和创意编程中。
Gemini 4 Carbon for cyber 带来了我们迄今最强的网络安全能力，为安全团队提供保护关键软件所需的端到端情报。通过 Fairwind Program 访问时，Carbon 在发现漏洞（SEC-bench Pro）、利用漏洞（ExploitGym）和修补漏洞（CWE-bench v1）等关键基准上领先：检查软件、追踪缺陷如何跨系统串联，并生成经过验证的根因补丁。
Google 内外的早期测试者已经在实践中看到 Carbon for cyber 的出色效果。
Gemini 4 Carbon 在物理、数学和生命科学领域的推理表现显著提升，能够综合实验数据、检验假设，并逐步推理多步骤的领域难题。对药物毒性研究公司 Axiom Bio 而言，Carbon 目前是转化科学领域性能领先的模型，发现了他们此前未曾发现的新型毒性机制。Axiom 正将生产环境的科学分析和智能体迁移到 Carbon 与 Argon 上，以加速更安全药物的研发。
Google 各团队的研究人员已在 Google Antigravity 中使用 Carbon 来加速工作：
四周前，我们开放了申请通道，让 1 万名科学家在 Google Antigravity 中免费使用 Argon 六个月，以加快他们的研究进度，目前已有数千名科学家完成接入。今天，我们将把 Carbon 的使用权限扩展到现有和未来的参与者，并且今后该计划会持续提供对我们最新前沿模型的访问权限。申请通道 仍然开放 ，接入按每周滚动进行，需符合资格、容量和筛选要求。
随着每一款新模型发布，我们都会根据模型能力同步加强安全与保障缓解措施、智能体滥用防范、模型对齐和危害削减。
由于 Gemini 4 Carbon 引入了更强的网络能力，我们在 Argon 的 强大安全与保障体系 基础上进一步加固，以增强对滥用和提示词注入的抵御能力。
查看 模型卡 ，了解 Gemini 4 Carbon 的更多信息并开始基于它开发；也可以浏览我们更

items.title: Wiz 讲解如何评估 AI 智能体的网络安全能力
items.description: Wiz Research 介绍其 Cyber Model Arena v3.9 的基准设计方法，该基准覆盖 26 个模型、59 个智能体和 327 道挑战，分代码漏洞、API 安全、Web 安全和云安全四类。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/momr4yrt6hhhfeuzjfqz6ryqy
items.excerpt:
How to Evaluate AI Agent Cybersecurity Capabilities
Wiz Research 介绍其 Cyber Model Arena v3.9 的基准设计方法，该基准覆盖 26 个模型、59 个智能体和 327 道挑战，分代码漏洞、API 安全、Web 安全和云安全四类。
Wiz 研究人员分享了自建网络安全智能体基准的设计原则与踩坑经验，解释了为何用确定性代码评分替代 LLM 评委并隔离防作弊。
许多公司已经在自己的开发和部署生态中使用智能体，而攻击者有时会利用成群的攻击型智能体同时攻击数千家公司。为了帮助防御方为这个新时代做好准备，我们需要一个能比较这些智能体能力的评分。正因如此重要，学术界和业界的实验室都开始着手研究如何衡量，并制定正确衡量的标准，所以这个话题既及时又日益相关。
在本文中，我将分享 Wiz 在重新推出 Cyber Model Arena 时，为应对这一基准测试要务所遵循的关键原则。完整的方法论、我们的评分方式以及任务收集过程 可供下载 。截至本文撰写时，Wiz Cyber Model Arena v3.9 包含 26 个模型、4 个通用执行框架、59 个智能体、327 个挑战，每个挑战有三次尝试机会，每次限时 1,000 秒（这些数字还在不断增长）。
要创建基准测试，先确定基准目标。然后围绕它构建任务、环境和度量方式。我将在本文后面详细展开这一点，并解释指导整个流程的原则。
选对任务。 在写第一个任务之前，先确定 为什么 （目标）、 是什么 （数据、标准答案和智能体配置）以及 怎么做 （指标、评估函数）。尽可能从真实分布中构建数据，而不是用 AI 生成或 AI 标注的任务。
用代码评分，而不是用 LLM。 直接、确定性地衡量成功，并采取防作弊措施：将智能体与服务器和互联网隔离，不给它任何查答案的途径。除非设计良好、经过校准且没有偏差，否则不要依赖 LLM 作为评判者。
让评估尽可能贴近真实。 把 执行框架和模型放在一起 评估，给智能体不止一次尝试机会，并权衡成功与解题成本。
避开常见陷阱。 LLM 评判、样本量小、任务不均衡、只评估模型以及答案泄露，都会让基准测试不可靠。而且要从小的开始：一个执行框架、一个快速且便宜的模型、几个任务和一个简单的评分器。等跑通了再扩大规模。
大多数公开的网络安全智能体基准测试回答的，并不是防御方所问的那个问题。选择题测验衡量的是模型知识，而非生产环境表现；由另一个模型评判 LLM 输出，衡量的是两者之间的一致性，而非成功与否。我们要回答的是：智能体能否执行一次真实的攻击。
写下你的基准测试必须回答的那一个问题，并用它来检验之后的每一个决定。我们的问题是：
仅给定任务指令、一个通用智能体脚手架、1,000 秒的时间预算，且没有外部知识来源，智能体能否在真实目标上产生可验证的效果？
Wiz Research 的 《2026 年云端 AI 现状报告》 发现，至少 57% 的组织已经部署了自托管的 AI 智能体技术，而在观测到的云环境中，至少 80% 出现了 MCP 服务器。人们已经在采购这类系统，也已经在针对它们做防御。这就是 为什么 。本文余下的部分讲的是，如何构建一个服务于这个目的的数字。
为什么。 防御方或采购方应当能够依据这个数字采取行动。“更高的 pass@1”不是为什么。“这个智能体在交付状态下，仅凭指令能否攻破一个真实目标？”才是。
是什么。 明确被评估的对象。在这里，它是由攻击者运行的智能体（模型 + 运行框架 + 工具 + 系统提示词），这也是我们采用贴近现实的限制条件的原因：1,000 秒、三次尝试、简单的系统提示词，并且可以访问客户端代码但不能访问服务端代码。
怎么做。 基准测试为每个样例报告一个单一的底线指标很重要。要把众多相互竞争的指标归结为一个数字，就选 一个优化指标 ，把其余一切都当作 满足性约束 。如果你有五个相互竞争的指标，又无法把它们归结起来，那么哪个智能体更好就会变成一场关于指标的争论。
基准测试只能代表它所包含的任务。只采样困难任务，你衡量的就不再是工作中的成功率，而是困难任务上的成功率。而一个仅凭单一任务类别就声称衡量“攻击能力”的基准测试，是言过其实的。
因此，我们从现实中已经存在的来源构建了四个权重相等的类别。我们没有用 LLM 生成或标注任务。
智能体在不同类别之间的表现差异很大。对 59 个智能体取平均，pass@1 在 API 安全上为 78.0%，Web 上为 64.6%，云上为 56.5%，代码漏洞上为 38.2%。总排名第一的智能体在 Web 上得 74.7%，在代码上得 65.8%（而 Web 最高可达 90.8%）。另一个智能体在代码上只得 9.7%，在 API 上仍有 71.6%。
规模也很重要。近期许多网络安全基准测试的任务数不足 30 个。在 50% 的成功率下，30 个任务给出的 95% 置信区间约为 ±18 个百分点，因此一个比另一个高 15 分的智能体未必就更好。
真实标注是评估的基础。用 LLM 作为评判者来打分一直是标准做法，但评判者并不直接衡量成功。它们有偏差（往往偏好第一个选项）、有随机性（每次运行结果不同）、昂贵且缓慢，而且要想在长期使用的基准测试中使用它们，必须先做校准和去偏。当你使用评判者时，你衡量的是某个 LLM 是否认为智能体成功了。这个差异是系统里内嵌的一笔债。
我们改用代码来评判。每道题都设计成会留下可核查的痕迹，或输出精确的结构化结果，智能体退出后由确定性的评分器检查。代码评分器成本低、可重复运行，也不是需要校准的模型。
只要有机会，智能体就会走捷径：上网查答案、从磁盘上读现成解法，或者操纵评分器。如果分数是在能联网搜索、能查 CVE 数据库、文件夹里还写着题目名称的条件下拿到的，那衡量的就是别的东西了：究竟是完成了任务，还是攻破了任务。 CTFusion 仅仅放宽了联网搜索权限，解题率就变化了多达 12 个百分点。
至于数据

items.title: A unifying voice
items.description: Warehouses are becoming more automated by the day, with many combining an ever-wider selection of material handling equipment and technology designed to speed and streamline operations. Experts say collaborative robots, wearable technologies, autonomous forklifts, and automated storage and retrieval systems (AS/RS) are coming together like never before in a single facility as companies take a “best-of-breed” approach to automating for current and future needs. But how do warehouse workers connect to all of those technologies to create efficient and effective workflows throughout the facility?
items.excerpt:
Voice-directed solutions are helping workers move seamlessly among a growing array of material handling technologies on the warehouse floor.
Victoria Kickham, Senior Editor , started her career as a newspaper reporter in the Boston area before moving into B2B journalism. She has covered manufacturing, distribution, and supply chain issues for a variety of publications in the industrial and electronics sectors, and now writes about warehousing, transportation, and logistics trends for DC VELOCITY . Victoria earned a bachelor’s degree in English from the University of New Hampshire and a master’s degree in English from Northeastern University.
Warehouses are becoming more automated by the day, with many combining an ever-wider selection of material handling equipment and technology designed to speed and streamline operations. Experts say collaborative robots, wearable technologies, autonomous forklifts, and automated storage and retrieval systems (AS/RS) are coming together like never before in a single facility as companies take a “best-of-breed” approach to automating for current and future needs.
But how do warehouse workers connect to all of those technologies to create efficient and effective workflows throughout the facility?
Voice-directed technology may just be the answer. Long used primarily as a picking solution, voice technology is now used for many other workflows, such as receiving and putaway, and is increasingly functioning as an interface between human workers and the various machines they interact with during the course of that work. The trend highlights a shift occurring in warehouse automation strategy that emphasizes the value of humans and machines working side by side, according to Joshua Franker, head of marketing for voice technology and warehouse optimization software company Lucas Systems . That shift signals a move away from an earlier strategy that was focused on reducing labor by turning warehouses into robot-dominated facilities.
“Instead, the focus is how do we create the most efficient and accurate versions [of a facility]—knowing that humans are still a part of it?” Franker says. “Robots and humans all working well together—how do we do that and create the most efficient and accurate warehouse [operations] that we can?”
Franker and others say voice technology is taking a front seat on that journey.

items.title: Texas’s Energy Reset: The Supply Chain Consequences for Houston
items.description: An election can change the direction of government overnight. Changing the direction of an industrial economy takes considerably longer. That distinction matters in Houston, where oil and gas production, refining, petrochemicals, engineering, and international trade form one of the world’s most interconnected industrial ecosystems. Texas voters delivered a historic political realignment on November 3, 2026. […] The post Texas’s Energy Reset: The Supply Chain Consequences for Houston appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
An election can change the direction of government overnight. Changing the direction of an industrial economy takes considerably longer. That distinction matters in Houston, where oil and gas production, refining, petrochemicals, engineering, and international trade form one of the world’s most interconnected industrial ecosystems.
Texas voters delivered a historic political realignment on November 3, 2026. According to the Texas Secretary of State’s official election results , Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Governor Greg Abbott. At the same time, Democrats captured the lieutenant governorship, attorney general’s office, control of the Texas House, and a seat on the Railroad Commission. James Talarico also won election to the U.S. Senate.
For Houston’s energy industry, the election introduces a different regulatory and investment environment. However, the immediate supply chain risk is not necessarily reduced energy production or even total capital spending. It is a change in the timing, location, and composition of industrial investment, a distinction that deserves considerably more attention than the political headlines.
Houston’s energy economy extends far beyond drilling. Refineries, chemical plants, pipelines, export terminals, power infrastructure, and manufacturing facilities depend on an extensive network of suppliers and transportation providers. These operations represent decades of investment in physical assets that cannot simply be relocated in response to an election. Nevertheless, political decisions influence the economics of maintaining, expanding, and modernizing those assets.
One important change involves the Texas Railroad Commission, which regulates oil and gas production. Democrat Jon Rosenthal, an oilfield engineer with more than two decades of experience, won the election after advocating stronger enforcement, restrictions on routine flaring, improved well-plugging programs, and additional oversight of wastewater disposal.
The commission will retain a Republican majority, limiting Rosenthal’s ability to implement significant changes without support from his colleagues. Republicans also retained control of the Texas Senate, with a 19–12 majority, despite Democratic gains elsewhere.

items.title: Introducing AlphaProof Code: a breakthrough in verifying complex software at depth
items.description: AlphaProof Code agents wrote three million lines of proofs in Lean to verify Signal’s core encryption.
items.excerpt:
How Google DeepMind researchers built a new agentic framework that formally verified the code of Signal’s cryptographic protocol — long considered to be a grand security challenge
Today, we’re sharing a milestone in software security long considered to be a grand challenge: Google DeepMind researchers guided AI agents to mathematically prove key security properties of the actual code underlying the Signal protocol, the technology that protects billions of private conversations in apps like Signal and Google Messages.
This breakthrough discovery was made using AlphaProof Code , a novel agentic framework for formal verification at unprecedented depth that combines human expertise with AI agents. Formal verification—mathematically proving code runs correctly without flaws—is the highest standard of security assurance; however, it is difficult and often labor-intensive.
Our work marks the first time AI has been used to formally verify a widely deployed cryptographic protocol at this depth. It's also the first time the implementation of a widely deployed protocol like this has been formally verified by any method, with or without AI.
AlphaProof Code is a multi-LLM agentic framework that splits the work of formal verification the way a research team would: human experts work with AI to decide what to prove, and a group of AI agents does it.
First, our researchers collaborated with a mix of models to translate Signal’s security goals into formal mathematical specifications, with human experts reviewing every one. From there, agents powered by Gemini Carbon did the proofs, generating over six million lines of Lean, a computer language that mathematically proves the accuracy of code.
Next, the agents audited the proof and highlighted areas that needed a second look by a human – just one percent of the codebase, a massive time savings. Because Lean automatically checks the rest, our experts could focus their review where human judgment matters most.
Cryptographic protocols underpin nearly all digital communication, from online banking to web browsing, and a single flaw can expose millions of people at once. That's why experts have spent decades formally analyzing them.
But most protocol verification stops at the design level. Our agents went further, proving that the compiled code fulfills the key security properties – such as keeping messages protected before and after a device is temporarily compromised – down to the exact code running on devices.
